cli.stop_help.stop.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.stop_help.stop.note: Top-level summary: stopping requests graceful completion before escalating to signals. Keep lop as the executable name.

cli.stop_help.target.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.stop_help.target.note: Positional matching selector, not a path requirement: conversation name, session id, pid, or cwd substring; matching ignores case.

cli.stop_help.pid.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.stop_help.pid.note: --pid selects only the exact numeric process identifier. Preserve the flag token.

cli.stop_help.session.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.stop_help.session.note: --session selects the exact session identifier, not a fuzzy name match.

cli.stop_help.all.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.stop_help.all.note: --all targets this machine only. TTY is a terminal; preserve --yes as the confirmation-bypass flag.

cli.stop_help.yes.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.stop_help.yes.note: --yes bypasses the --all confirmation and is mandatory when stdin is not a terminal. Preserve --all and stdin tokens.

cli.stop_help.json.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.stop_help.json.note: --json emits one machine-readable outcome per target rather than a single aggregate outcome.

cli.stop_help.timeout.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.stop_help.timeout.note: --timeout is the per-session graceful operation wait before escalation, with a default of 10 seconds.

cli.stop_help.force.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.stop_help.force.note: Safety caveat for --force: unverified socket identity, a running turn, and an already-signalled departure may be interrupted. Plain stop already handles cooperative mid-turn runtimes promptly through their socket.
